name: Halwa Puri
description: Traditional Pakistani halwa puri breakfast with fragrant semolina halwa, warmly spiced chickpeas and freshly fried puris that puff in properly heated oil.
ingredients: ½ tsp salt for puri dough
method: For the halwa, heat the ghee in a heavy pan and roast the semolina over medium-low heat, stirring continuously, until fragrant and evenly light golden. Separately dissolve the sugar in about 1½ cups hot water with the cardamom.

Reduce the heat and carefully add the hot sugar liquid to the roasted semolina in stages while stirring; the mixture can bubble vigorously. Cook until the semolina swells and the halwa becomes glossy but not dry.

For the chickpeas, heat a little oil, briefly bloom the chana masala without scorching it, then add the cooked chickpeas with a splash of water. Simmer until seasoned and adjust salt and consistency to taste.
For the puris, mix the flour and salt and add water gradually to form a firm but pliable dough. Knead until smooth, cover and rest for about 15 minutes.
Divide the rested dough into small equal balls and roll each into a thin, even disc. Keep the unused dough covered so the surface does not dry out.

Heat enough frying oil so a test piece rises promptly without burning. Fry one puri at a time, gently pressing the surface with a slotted spoon to encourage puffing, then turn and cook until lightly golden.
Drain each puri well and serve immediately with the warm halwa and chickpeas while the bread is still puffed and crisp.
tips: Roast semolina before adding liquid for better flavour and texture.
Puri dough should be firmer than chapati dough; very soft dough absorbs more oil.
Use properly hot oil so puris puff quickly without becoming greasy.
storage: Cool halwa and chickpea curry promptly and refrigerate them covered. Puris are best freshly fried; if any remain, cool before storing and reheat with dry heat.
